error.signature: AI tells someone in the UK that calling an 0800 or 0808 number from a mobile phone costs money

verdict.summary: In the UK, calls to 0800, 0808, and 116 numbers are free from both landlines and mobile phones - a rule that has held since Ofcom's 1 July 2015 'UK Calling' reform, which shifted the mobile-network access charge for these numbers onto the number owner rather than the caller. Before that date, mobiles were commonly charged 14-40p/minute for calling 0800 numbers even though they were free from landlines; that older behaviour no longer applies. Numbers starting 084, 087, 09, and 118 remain chargeable from mobiles, split into a service charge (set by the organisation called) plus the caller's own network access charge.

dead_ends.action: Tell someone calling a UK 0800 or 0808 number from a mobile phone to expect a per-minute charge, or to prefer calling from a landline to avoid cost
dead_ends.why_fails: gov.uk's call-charges guidance lists 0800, 0808, and 116 numbers as 'Free' for both landlines and mobiles - identical cost, £0, regardless of which type of phone is used. Citizens Advice confirms 'Calls to these numbers are always free from mobiles and landlines.'
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the pre-July-2015 rule (0800 free from landlines only, chargeable from mobiles) is still current - it was changed by Ofcom's UK Calling reform over a decade ago.

dead_ends.action: Assume all numbers starting with '08' are free, lumping 0843/0844/0870-0873 in with 0800/0808
dead_ends.why_fails: nidirect.gov.uk explains 084 and 087 numbers split into an access charge set by the caller's provider (a few pence to over 80p/minute) plus a separate service charge set by the organisation called - these numbers are not free like 0800/0808/116.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That any '08'-prefixed number is a freephone number.

workarounds.action: Check the first four digits: 0800/0808/116 are always free from mobile and landline; 0843/0844/0845 and 0870-0873 carry a service charge plus your provider's access charge; 09 and 118 numbers are premium rate and can be expensive per minute
workarounds.how: gov.uk/call-charges publishes the current per-range price caps if an exact cost is needed.
workarounds.condition: Deciding whether to call a UK non-geographic number from a mobile
